Class Window

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.slotkit.api.window.Window
public final class Window extends Object
The entry point to the window: where a consumer gets a typed handle to set or read behavior on anything addressable.

Menu-independent and menu-bound

A created slot has one address everywhere it appears (nested under its panel's id), so its handle needs no menu and is reached statically through slot(Address). A panel's own visibility and opacity are the panel's (Panel.visibleWhen, opaque), not the window's.

Only a vanilla slot is identified by its position in a live menu, so addressing one by index needs that menu: view(AbstractContainerMenu) returns the menu-bound WindowView for slot(int) and the rest.

      public static SlotHandle slot(com.trevlar.menukit.api.panel.ModeScope scope, Address address)
      A handle on the slot address names, declaring for scope: its gate, binding and operations apply while the acting player's mode is in that scope. Window.slot(ModeScope.SURVIVAL, a).gate(g) plus Window.slot(ModeScope.BOTH, a).gate(h) is "g in survival, h otherwise".
